scenes.heading: Writing a contract that protects your VA business

sents.d: Writing a contract that protects your VA business
A clear agreement protects against scope confusion and unpaid overtime.
A VA contract should define which tasks are included, monthly hour allotment if on retainer, what happens with hours worked beyond that allotment, and payment terms and timing.
Given the access-sensitive nature of VA work, a confidentiality clause covering client information, passwords, and business details you'll have access to is a standard and expected inclusion.
Including a notice period for ending the arrangement (e.g. two weeks) on both sides protects your income from a sudden loss of hours and gives you time to plan around a client's transition.

take: Cover tasks, hours, confidentiality and notice in your contract.
